about: PRD 50 (feature PR #51 and its sub-PRs #54, #56, #57), as GitHub returned them to the retro’s reads, recorded 2026-09-25. Pull requests, their files and reviews were read through the GitHub connector and kept in the REST shape, trimmed to what the retro reads: no bodies, no patches. The trees and blobs at the merge SHA are the merge commit’s own git objects.
notRecorded: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/events — the connector cannot read issue events, so the replay does not know when #51 was marked ready.
Issue and review comments, commits and check runs of the sub-PRs.

* feat(kit): an outbox item may carry an intro and a punchline

The parser accepts '## The intro, for fun' and '## The punchline, for fun'
together, right after the two plain-words sections, and exposes them as
sections.introFun and sections.punchlineFun. funLineProblems holds a line to
the plain-words rules and 120 characters. A settled ledger written before
this still parses.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_013b9fhnjpaDKDxqLGF3cmdd

* feat(kit): renderOutboxItem writes an item's intro and punchline

Both or neither, right after the plain decision and before the options or
the person steps; one without the other is refused. An adopted item embeds
both in its settled entry.

* feat(kit): omni check outbox holds an open item's intro and punchline to the rules

checkItemText grades each line, when an open item carries them, with
funLineProblems: the plain-words rules and 120 characters at most, naming
the file and the section. The pair stays optional.

* feat(kit): omni item new takes introFun and punchlineFun

Both or neither. Each is held to funLineProblems by the input schema, so a
line over 120 characters or not in plain words is refused naming its field:
exit 2, nothing written or adopted. The rendered item, or the settled entry
under --adopt, carries both sections.

* feat(kit): a fallback pool of intros and punchlines for outbox questions

banter.mjs holds 28 intros and 28 punchlines and assignBanter, which serves
ids in the order given: each takes the line its id hashes to (32-bit
FNV-1a), skipping a line an earlier id took, and starting over once every
line is taken. The test holds every line to funLineProblems, keeps it off
people and teams, and lists the game words the pool may not name.

* feat(kit): an intro and a punchline around every question on the pull request comment

Every open and every adopted question now reads: heading, intro in italics,
the quoted question, punchline in italics, then its options, the steps a
person must take or the older decision line. The pair is the item's own
when it carries one, and the kit's pool's otherwise, served in question-number
order so two renders agree and a new question never moves an older one's
lines. The Answered section, the PRD issue's comment and the Slack note are
unchanged.

* feat(plugin): do-work writes an intro and a punchline for every item it raises

The Fields paragraph of step 3 names introFun and punchlineFun, with their
rules: one sentence (two short ones at most), 120 characters at most, plain
words, about the question, never about a person or a team, never mocking
whoever answers; the kit refuses one without the other. The exit-2 bullet now
tells the two refusals apart: the JSON refused (one line on stderr naming the
field, stdout empty even with --json) and the rendered item refused (outcome
null with a reason).

* docs(plugin): do-work's Step 0 says the kit is not installed, not "not terraformed"

The plan asks that this SKILL.md name no game word, and "terraform" is one.
The other skills and the config error keep the old word; outbox item
s3-01-installed-not-terraformed (medium, not adopted in-wave) asks a person
whether to keep, revert or widen the change. It carries no intro or punchline
(spec decision 7).
